title: Localizing A[x_1..x_r]/(f_1x_1+...+f_rx_r-1) at f_i gives a polynomial ring over A_{f_i}
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\ge1$, $f_1,\dots,f_r\in A$, and $B=A[x_1,\dots,x_r]/(f_1x_1+\dots+f_rx_r-1)$ (quotient of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] by the principal ideal; $ ar x_j$ the class of $x_j$). Fix $i\in\{1,\dots,r\}$; let $A_{f_i}$ be the localization of $A$ at $\{1,f_i,f_i^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $B_{f_i}$ the localization of $B$ at the powers of the image of $f_i$, and regard $B_{f_i}$ as an $A_{f_i}$-algebra via the ring map $A_{f_i}	o B_{f_i}$, $a/f_i^e\mapsto a/f_i^e$ (induced by $A	o B$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property]). Let $A_{f_i}[y_j:j
e i]$ be the polynomial ring over $A_{f_i}$ in the $r-1$ variables $y_j$, $j\in\{1,\dots,r\}\setminus\{i\}$. Then the $A_{f_i}$-algebra homomorphism $A_{f_i}[y_j:j
e i]	o B_{f_i}$ with $y_j\mapsto  ar x_j/1$ is an isomorphism; its inverse sends $ ar x_j/1\mapsto y_j$ for $j
e i$ and $ ar x_i/1\mapsto f_i^{-1} igl(1-\sum_{j
e i}f_jy_j igr)$.

proof.text: (The map $\Phi$ and the structure map.) Write $g=f_1x_1+\dots+f_rx_r-1$, $\pi:A[x_1,\dots,x_r]\to B$ the quotient map, $\lambda:B\to B_{f_i}$, $b\mapsto b/1$, and $u=1/f_i\in A_{f_i}$, so $f_iu=1$. The image of $f_i$ in $B_{f_i}$ is a unit, so by the universal property of localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] the composite $A\to B\to B_{f_i}$ extends uniquely to a ring map $\alpha:A_{f_i}\to B_{f_i}$ with $\alpha(a/f_i^e)=a/f_i^e$; this is the $A_{f_i}$-algebra structure of the statement. By the universal property of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] over $A_{f_i}$ there is a unique $A_{f_i}$-algebra map $\Phi:A_{f_i}[y_j:j\ne i]\to B_{f_i}$ with $\Phi(y_j)=\bar x_j/1$ ($j\ne i$): this is the map of the statement.

proof.text:
(The map $\Psi$.) Let $C=A_{f_i}[y_j:j
e i]$ and $z=u igl(1-\sum_{j
e i}f_jy_j igr)\in C$ (coefficients $f_j$ read in $A_{f_i}$ via $a\mapsto a/1$). By the universal property of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] over $A$ ($C$ an $A$-algebra via $A	o A_{f_i}	o C$) there is a unique $A$-algebra map $\psi_0:A[x_1,\dots,x_r]	o C$ with $\psi_0(x_j)=y_j$ for $j
e i$ and $\psi_0(x_i)=z$. Then $\psi_0(g)=f_iz+\sum_{j
e i}f_jy_j-1=f_iu igl(1-\sum_{j
e i}f_jy_j igr)+\sum_{j
e i}f_jy_j-1=0$, since $f_iu=1$. Hence $\psi_0$ kills the ideal $(g)$ and factors through the quotient: $\psi_0=\psi_1\circ\pi$ for a unique ring map $\psi_1:B	o C$ (universal property of a quotient ring, i.e. the homomorphism theorem). $\psi_1( ar f_i)=f_i/1$ is a unit of $C$ (inverse $u$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] $\psi_1$ extends uniquely to a ring map $\Psi:B_{f_i}	o C$ with $\Psi\circ\lambda=\psi_1$, $\Psi(b/f_i^e)=\psi_1(b)u^e$. In particular $\Psi( ar x_j/1)=y_j$ for $j
e i$ and $\Psi( ar x_i/1)=f_i^{-1} igl(1-\sum_{j
e i}f_jy_j igr)$, the formulas of the statement. $\Psi$ is $A_{f_i}$-linear: $\Psi(\alpha(a/f_i^e))=\Psi( ar a/f_i^e)=(a/1)u^e=a/f_i^e$, i.e. $\Psi\circ\alpha$ is the structure map $A_{f_i}	o C$.

proof.text: ($\Psi\circ\Phi=\mathrm{id}$.) $\Psi\circ\Phi:C\to C$ is an $A_{f_i}$-algebra map (both are, step 1 and step 2) with $\Psi(\Phi(y_j))=\Psi(\bar x_j/1)=y_j$ for every $j\ne i$; the identity of $C$ has the same values, so $\Psi\circ\Phi=\mathrm{id}_C$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

proof.text:
($\Phi\circ\Psi=\mathrm{id}$, conclusion.) Consider the two ring maps $\Phi\circ\Psi\circ\lambda\circ\pi$ and $\lambda\circ\pi$ from $A[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ to $B_{f_i}$; both are $A$-algebra maps ($\Phi\circ\Psi\circ\lambda\circ\pi=\Phi\circ\psi_0$, and $\Phi$ is $A_{f_i}$-linear, hence $A$-linear). On $x_j$, $j
e i$: $\Phi(\psi_0(x_j))=\Phi(y_j)= ar x_j/1$. On $x_i$: $\Phi(\psi_0(x_i))=\Phi(z)=\alpha(u) igl(1-\sum_{j
e i} ar f_j ar x_j/1 igr)$, and in $B$ the relation $ ar g=0$ gives $1-\sum_{j
e i} ar f_j ar x_j= ar f_i ar x_i$, so $\Phi(z)=\alpha(u)\alpha(f_i/1)( ar x_i/1)= ar x_i/1$ since $\alpha(u)\alpha(f_i/1)=\alpha(1)=1$. So the two maps agree on all variables and are equal by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Since $\pi$ is surjective, $\Phi\circ\Psi\circ\lambda=\lambda$, and by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] (both $\Phi\circ\Psi$ and $\mathrm{id}$ are ring maps $B_{f_i}	o B_{f_i}$ extending $\lambda$) $\Phi\circ\Psi=\mathrm{id}_{B_{f_i}}$. With step 3, $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of $A_{f_i}$-algebras with inverse $\Psi$, which has the values on $ ar x_j/1$ computed in step 2.

lean.statement: theorem linearEquationLocalizationPolynomial (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (i : Fin r) : let I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A) := Ideal.span {(∑ j : Fin r, C (f j) * X j) - 1} let B := MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ I let q := Ideal.Quotient.mk I let Af := Localization.Away (f i) let Bf := Localization.Away (algebraMap A B (f i)) letI : Algebra Af Bf := (Localization.awayMap (algebraMap A B) (f i)).toAlgebra let x : Fin r → Bf := fun j ↦ algebraMap B Bf (q (X j)) ∃ e : MvPolynomial {j : Fin r // j ≠ i} Af ≃ₐ[Af] Bf, e.toAlgHom = aeval (fun j ↦ x j.1) ∧ (∀ j : {j : Fin r // j ≠ i}, e.symm (x j.1) = X j) ∧ e.symm (x i) = C (IsLocalization.Away.invSelf (S := Af) (f i)) * (1 - ∑ j : {j : Fin r // j ≠ i}, C (algebraMap A Af (f j.1)) * X j)
